raw_response:
I will still do wheat-maize on the same 3 mu, same as most years, because this land and our water well fit that system best. I do not like making big changes at my age. On only 3 mu, every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too much and lose yield, that hurts more. So I will keep the fertilizer a little on the safe side, close to what we have used in our area when fields look strong. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the base fertilizer down before sowing, and give three irrigations if the year is normal: one after sowing or for overwintering moisture, one at jointing, and one at grain filling if the soil is dry. Wheat needs more care through the cold season, so I will spray about twice, mainly for weeds and then for disease or aphids if they show. After wheat harvest, time is tight for maize, so I will seed hybrid maize quickly and keep the soil work simple. I will use a bit less phosphorus on maize than on wheat, keep nitrogen solid, and give two irrigations with the well if rain is not enough. For maize I will also spray about twice, usually once for weeds early and once later if armyworm or leaf disease shows. I do what has worked on nearby fields: steady inputs, no fancy changes, protect the yield first, and keep the spending within what a small household can carry.
